elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered still provides that the Agreement "shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date"; renewal is automatic, so the conditional automatic-renewal elements must all be satisfied, and the reminder and 30-day opt-out elements are not.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — a 12-month renewal term, within the limit and unchanged by the redline.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause requires "sixty (60) days written notice" to prevent renewal; 60 > 30, so the preferred opt-out window is not achieved (fallback level only).

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in Section 4.1 or the rendered text; the margin comment expressly leaves the reminder mechanic unaddressed, and a promise in a comment is not operative language.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Section 3.1 fixes consideration at "thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month" and Section 4.1 contains no renewal uplift or repricing mechanic, so no price increase is permitted on renewal.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Redlined Section 4.1 reads "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon sixty (60) days written notice to the other" — the Company can stop the annual auto-renewal on exactly 60 days' notice, at the fallback ceiling; deterministic check "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days" ok.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not engaged — the fee is a fixed 30% Net Sales share under Section 3.1 with no renewal-linked uplift, so no cap is required. Note the mapping's "already_met" quote of Section 3.1 is a fee-calculation clause, not a price cap; the element passes only because the condition is inapplicable.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single parameter change (ninety → sixty days) brings the non-renewal notice window inside the 60-day fallback ceiling, and the price-increase element is inapplicable because no renewal uplift mechanic exists.

Preferred level is not reached: there is no operative 60-day pre-renewal reminder obligation on HDI and the exit window is 60 rather than 30 days. To reach preferred the drafter would need to insert an express reminder duty ("HDI shall notify the Company in writing at least sixty (60) days before each renewal") and reduce the Company's notice to thirty (30) days.

Minimality holds: one numeral was amended inside the target element; the one-year renewal term, the "Termination Date" definition, Section 3.1 economics and all other wording are untouched, and no survival tails, procedures or extra requirements were added.

Caveat on retained-benefit: Section 4.1 is mutual, so shortening the window also lets HDI exit on 60 rather than 90 days' notice. That is an unavoidable consequence of editing a symmetrical clause and is not treated as a minimality failure, but if preserving the longer notice from HDI matters commercially, consider an asymmetric formulation (Company may prevent renewal on sixty (60) days' notice; HDI's notice remains ninety (90) days).
Intent preserved: no undefined terms, dangling cross-references or contradictory retained sentences result; the notice-content sentence defining "Termination Date" continues to operate.
Claimed status "deviation" is correct — the original ninety-day window failed the fallback maximum, so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale-only note.
